correction.text: the kingdom of Croatia and Dalmatia in personal union with Hungary: Croatia, Dalmatia and Slavonia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row for the union: its Kingdom of Croatia ends in 1098 and the Kingdom of Hungary shapes draw Croatia inside Hungary). 'Coloman was crowned in Biograd in 1102'; the kingdom 'entered a personal union with the Kingdom of Hungary in 1102'; Slavonia had been conquered in 1091. The page gives no area; the modern country Croatia (about 56,600 km2) is a rough stand-in, with Istria, Ragusa and the Međimurje not separated.

region.text: the kingdom of Croatia and Dalmatia in personal union with Hungary: Croatia, Dalmatia and Slavonia

ledger.note: 1102: Coloman is crowned at Biograd and Croatia enters a personal union with Hungary. 'Coloman was crowned in Biograd in 1102'; 'entered a personal union with the Kingdom of Hungary in 1102'; 'In 1102, after a succession crisis, the crown passed into the hands of the Árpád dynasty.'

region.text: Biograd, Split, Trogir, Šibenik and Zadar

ledger.note: 1116: Venice takes the coastal cities. 'In 1116, after the death of Coloman, Venice attacked the Dalmatian coast' and seized Biograd, Split, Trogir, Šibenik and Zadar; in 1117 Stephen II 'unsuccessfully tried to regain the lost cities'.

minus.text: Biograd, Split, Trogir, Šibenik and Zadar

ledger.note: 1133: Béla II 'won back the lost cities except Zadar'.
1167: 'a part of Croatia south of Krka River' falls to the Byzantines, who held it until 1180.
1180: the Byzantine hold on southern Croatia ends ('held it until 1180').

region.text: the land between the Cetina and the Neretva (western Hum)

ledger.note: Around 1327-1329: 'Stephen II Kotromanić annexed the land between the Cetina and Neretva' (western Hum, 'not always in Croatia's possession'). The page dates it only by context, so the year is the start of the span.

region.text: all Venetian possessions in Dalmatia, from the Kvarner to the Bay of Kotor

ledger.note: 18 February 1358: the Treaty of Zadar. Venice had to give 'all its possessions in Dalmatia to the King, from the Kvarner to the Bay of Kotor' and drop Dalmatia from the doge's title; Croatia and Dalmatia are named in the plural from 1359 (Croatia page).

1409: 'Eventually in 1409 Ladislaus sold his rights in Dalmatia to Venice for 100,000 ducats'; 'until Venice regained the Dalmatian coast in 1409'. The Treaty of Zadar page says only that Zadar 'was later sold back to Venice by Ladislaus of Naples' without date.

1482: 'they conquered large parts of Herzegovina in 1482'; the Ottomans 'also took Croatian strongholds in the Neretva valley'. Year from the page; the region is the Neretva valley county as my reading.
29 May 1522: Knin falls ('captured it on 29 May 1522'), the seat of Petar Snačić and later of Ivan Nelipić.

wars.name: Venetian conquest of the Dalmatian coast

zones.text: Biograd, Split, Trogir, Šibenik and Zadar

wars.outcome: Venice seized Biograd, Split, Trogir, Šibenik and Zadar in 1116; Béla II won back all but Zadar in 1133.

wars.name: Byzantine conquest of southern Croatia
wars.outcome: The Byzantines held the part of Croatia south of the Krka until 1180.

wars.name: Fourth Crusade, sack of Zadar
wars.outcome: Venetians and crusaders sacked Zadar in 1202; no territory change is dated on the page.

wars.name: Hungarian-Venetian war ended by the Treaty of Zadar
wars.outcome: Venice ceded 'all its possessions in Dalmatia' from the Kvarner to the Bay of Kotor on 18 February 1358.
wars.note: The war's years are not on the page; only the treaty year is used.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of southern Croatia
wars.outcome: Neretva strongholds 1482; the Croatian army was intercepted at Krbava Field on 9 September 1493; Knin fell on 29 May 1522; the Croatian estates chose Ferdinand at Cetin on 1 January 1527.

certainty.note: The page gives lists of cities and rivers (Krka, Cetina, Neretva), not boundaries; the 1358 treaty cession 'from the Kvarner to the Bay of Kotor' is the only line-like description.

notes:
Croatia in union with Hungary is a state Cliopatria lacks (eu-15-c asked for it; the Kingdom of Hungary dossier ends in 1546 and draws Croatia inside Hungary). The modern country Croatia is a rough base shape: Istria, the Međimurje and Dubrovnik/Ragusa (Cliopatria's Republic of Ragusa 1385-1808) are not separated, and Slavonia is the north-east of the same shape. No page opened gives an area, a capital or a boundary; capitals is empty because the Croatia page says 'Capital(s): not stated' (the union was ruled from Hungary).

Not settled: (1) the Dalmatian coast 1180-1357 and 1409-1526: the Croatia page names only the Zadar sack of 1202; the 1358 treaty shows Venice held 'all its possessions in Dalmatia' before it, so the Hungarian hold in 1180-1357 was lower than the keyframe shows; a gap-filler should open the Dalmatia or Venetian Dalmatia pages. (2) The Banate of Jajce and Srebrenik of 1463 (Matthias Corvinus, after the fall of Bosnia) are Hungarian banates in Bosnia, not clearly part of this kingdom; no event. (3) The division of the ban's office into Croatia-Dalmatia and Slavonia in 1225 (merged again by 1476) is administrative and gets no event. (4) Paul Šubić gained Bosnia in 1299 as ban; the page does not make it territory of this kingdom. (5) Kingdom of Slavonia page was thin (1699-1868 only). (6) After 1527 the Habsburg Kingdom of Croatia (and the Ottoman Bosnia/Slavonia conquests) needs a dossier. (7) Counterparts: byzantine-empire, republic-of-venice, banate-of-bosnia, ottoman-empire, habsburg-monarchy all exist as slugs.
